answer: A prism mapping service pays for storage of karst and inlet surveys in proportion to proven disk space, with no signup bonus. A sound proof-of-replication scheme gives each claim a distinct encoded replica; random audits demand timely proofs throughout the epoch. Ten aliases claiming ten replicas must retain ten replicas, not point to one shared file. More reward therefore needs more disk space and continued availability. This assumes encoding resists deduplication and fast recomputation; weak proofs permit fake capacity, and wealthy disk owners can still dominate.
